title: Sets [Unique Values]
description:
Now that we know how to structure objects and behavior, let's look at something just as important:

**How do we store collections of data?**

---
## Sets
A **Set** is a collection of values where:
- Every value is **unique**
- No duplicates are allowed

```ts
const users = new Set<string>();

users.add("alice");
users.add("bob");
users.add("alice"); // duplicate, ignored

console.log(users.size); // 2
```

Even though we added "alice" twice, it only exists once.

---
## Common Methods
- `.add(value)` -> adds a value
- `.has(value)` -> checks if it exists
- `.delete(value)` -> removes a value
- `.size` -> number of unique values

---
## Why use a Set?
Sets are perfect when:
- You want to **avoid duplicates**
- You only care if something exists

---
## Example
We want to track **unique users** who viewed a video.

Using an array could allow duplicates...
But a Set guarantees uniqueness.
NOTE: You can create a set using the contents of a array by instead of passing nothing to `new Set<T>()`, you pass the array to it.
